We consider here the use of a broader class of boundaries, called elastic, which involves one free parameter interpolating between these two limiting cases. We show how the conventional stochastic-$\delta N$, and its recently proposed time-reversed counterpart adapt to such a class of boundary behaviour. As an illustration, we solve time-reversed stochastic inflation for an exactly flat semi-infinite potential with an elastic boundary, a setup where the standard stochastic-$\delta N$ formalism breaks down, and compare the results to the purely absorbing case. Quantitative differences are found in terms of skewness and tail behaviour. This suggests that the transition between stochastic inflation and subsequent evolution may have observable consequences. Finally, we show that an elastic boundary stands as an effective model for stochastic tunnelling through a Dirac delta potential barrier. This mechanism can be equivalently framed as a smooth transition of stochastic trajectories in a mirror virtual medium with specific absorption properties.
papers.authors: Baptiste Blachier

papers.title: A Charged Compact Star Solution for a Conducting Sphere
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.42051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers the simplest charged stellar model, namely, a uniform density star with electric charge distributed on its surface. In this model, we treat the uniform density star as a conducting sphere, where all electric charges are uniformly distributed on the surface and represented by a delta function. We obtain an analytical solution for the background metric of the star spacetime and find that the pressure of the perfect fluid inside the star is directed inward (negative pressure) near the inner surface. This is because the repulsive force between surface electric charges requires an inward pressure to maintain equilibrium. However, when the charge becomes too large, the pressure of the ideal fluid at the stellar center gets directed outwards again. This is because the electric field itself is also a part of the stress energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$, acting as a source of gravity. When the gravitational effect of the electric field dominates, the perfect fluid must provide outward pressure to balance the inward gravitational attraction. On the other hand, we have also studied the axial perturbation in charged spacetimes using the finite difference method. We found that axial Maxwell perturbation and axial gravitational perturbation are coupled in the star spacetime, making it difficult to separate the variables by coordinate transformation. The computational results show that the waveforms of quasinormal modes vary with different charges.
papers.authors: Kai Lin

papers.title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.42056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work has shown that a simple form of coupled dark energy with a constant coupling produces a good fit to the DESI data. In this scenario, dark matter, but not baryons, couples to a scalar field, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle (EP). We first generalize the coupled dark energy model by adding a nonminimal coupling between the scalar field and gravity, and dub the resulting model "doubly coupled dark energy". We then construct a parameter $E_P$ in this model that quantifies EP violation on cosmological scales and can be measured with large galaxy surveys in a model-independent way. Finally, we forecast constraints on the couplings for present and future spectroscopic galaxy surveys, namely DESI, Euclid, and SKA Phase 2 (SKA2). To keep the analysis as general as possible, we leave the initial power spectrum shape and the galaxy bias free to vary in several bins. Among these surveys, SKA2 could provide the tightest constraint on the coupling strength in the coupled dark energy scenario, with a relative $1\sigma$ uncertainty of $22\%$. The constraints weaken when both couplings are varied, but can be further improved by increasing the number of galaxies detected.
papers.authors: Yannick Kegel, Ziyang Zheng, Luca Amendola

papers.title: Far-Zone Gravitational Interactions at the Sixth Post-Newtonian Order
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.42057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the nonlinear far-zone dynamics of compact binaries at the sixth post-Newtonian (6PN) order in the effective field theory of general relativity. We derive the complete $\mathcal{O}(G^2)$ far-zone action of a generic multipolar source in both the causal and the conservative prescriptions. Besides the known tails and failed tails, it contains five new sectors generated by the nonlinear memory of the emitted waves. On scattering orbits, they contain a boundary term, nonlocal in time, fixed by the balance of angular momentum. The same construction yields the emitted waveforms, whose energy and angular-momentum fluxes balance the losses of the action. For the binary, the 6PN dynamics also requires PN corrections to the lower-order sectors, the iterated radiation reaction, and a coupling quadratic in the curvature of the composite source, whose coefficient we fix by matching the gravitational Compton amplitude to that of the constituents. We compute the two-radiation contributions to the total scattering angle at fourth, fifth and sixth post-Minkowskian (PM) order and to the conservative angle at 4PM and 5PM, retaining the integer-PN terms through 6PN. For the conservative angle, we give both the local and $\gamma$-3 prescriptions. Combined with the tail and the known potential contributions, our results reproduce the conservative and total 4PM angles and the second-self-force part of the conservative 5PM angle. Including the dissipative tail, we recover the total 5PM angle through 5PN and determine its new 6PN coefficient. At 6PM, the two-radiation contribution to the total angle extends the known 5PN result to 6PN.
papers.authors: Giacomo Brunello

papers.title: Hyperbolic scaling of the small-exponent limit in magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.42091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A magnetic spacetime can approach Schwarzschild while its electromagnetic characteristics remain singular in the same parameter limit. We study this separation in fractional-power nonlinear electrodynamics as the exponent tends to zero with asymptotic mass, magnetic charge and nonlinear coupling independently fixed. The extraordinary polarization admits a common physical time direction only outside a boundary that grows as the inverse fourth root of the exponent. On this radial scale, the lapse tends to unity but the constitutive angular response retains a nondegenerate barrier and finite scaled critical data. An exact representation of the exterior electromagnetic energy yields complete second-order corrections to the orbit and impact, separating mass and charge contributions and their distinct cancellations. Constraining the mass to equal the electromagnetic self-energy preserves the leading critical constants while changing the approach from fourth-root to square-root corrections. Returning rays remain inside the admissible exterior and define a limiting scattering function with a calculated logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient. In the weak regime, constitutive bending decays as the inverse fourth power of scaled impact, whereas finite mass supplies a slower inverse-impact tail. We determine their competition scale, its accessibility above the critical impact, and the accuracy of the two-term approximation. Independent energy, orbit and scattering calculations check the expansions and resolve their parameter-dependent convergence. The analysis shows how a nearly vacuum background can support a distinct exterior optical limit through the nonlinear constitutive response.
papers.authors: Jonathan A. Rebou\c{c}as, R. Mart\'inez von Dossow, Edson Otoniel

papers.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
papers.abstract: arXiv:2610.42151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are an important source of systematic uncertainty in weak gravitational lensing measurements and also serve as a test for models of galaxy formation and evolution. These galaxy alignments are usually modeled assuming that the IA are sourced by the tidal fields around the galaxies. However, galaxy properties, like their proximity to other galaxies and their mass, provide alignment contributions beyond the tidal field. In this work, we perform novel model-agnostic tests to determine the impact of density-weighting on the IA of galaxies using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and SDSS-III (BOSS). We show that the primary effect of density-weighting is an increase of the alignment amplitude at large scales, whereas the small-scale impact is sample-dependent. We also assess the tidal alignment paradigm for IllustrisTNG galaxies using two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes, tidal fields, and the sampled background tidal field of the simulation box. We find, given the precision of our measurements, that central galaxies align linearly to the underlying (non-linear) tidal field well into the 1-halo regime.
papers.authors: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek, Rachel Mandelbaum, Hung-Jin Huang, Ananth Tenneti
